equity_bridge.item: Net unfunded AFFA asbestos liability, net of tax
equity_bridge.note: 10-Q 30 Sep 2026, note 9 rollforward. Already nets AICF restricted cash and investments, insurance receivables and the asbestos deferred tax asset. Book value is undiscounted, which is mildly conservative.

equity_bridge.item: Fermacell sale proceeds, net of tax and closure costs
equity_bridge.note: EUR 840m (about $980m, hedged with deal-contingent forwards) expected H1 calendar 2027, less an allowance of about $80m for tax on the gain, the $26m European fiber cement closure cost and closing adjustments. Europe is excluded from the flows. Not yet closed; a broken deal would replace this with a business earning about $40m of operating income a year.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: FY2027 guidance for year one, then mid-cycle housing recovery plus material conversion; historical CAGRs not used directly
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (13.8% over five years) diverges more than 30% from revenue CAGR (9.4%) and is not a usable anchor: equity was negative until FY2019 because of the asbestos provision and then tripled in FY2026 on stock issued for AZEK.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs are FY2019/FY2021 to FY2024 from the Metrics CSV, the pre-AZEK company. FCF is on the owner basis (reported FCF less SBC and equity-award withholding taxes; no interest strip, net debt throughout): FY2021 $658.2m to FY2024 $431.8m. The five-year owner-FCF CAGR is undefined because FY2019 was negative (-$26.0m) in a capacity-build year. Owner FCF fell while revenue grew because capex rose from 4% to 11-16% of sales. Since then: FY2025 revenue $3,877.5m (-1.5%), FY2026 $4,835.8m including nine months of AZEK.

scenario_narratives.base: FY2027 lands at the midpoint of reaffirmed guidance (continuing-operations net sales about $5.06bn, Adjusted EBITDA about $1.49bn, a 29.4% margin before SBC). The US housing market stays soft through FY2028 and then normalises, so growth runs 5-6% in FY2028-FY2031 on mid-cycle starts recovery, continued fiber-cement and composite share gain against wood and vinyl, and modest price, before fading to 3%. AZEK cost synergies and the Fontana/Summerville closures lift the margin about 2.5 points to 32% by year six; capex settles at 6-6.5% of sales once the capacity programme is digested. Asbestos is funded out of the bridge and the Fermacell sale completes on the announced terms.
scenario_narratives.bull: US single-family starts and repair-and-remodel recover from FY2028, the AZEK commercial synergies (siding dealers carrying TimberTech decking and the reverse) arrive on schedule, and Siding & Trim holds the mid-30s segment margin it printed in Q2 FY2027. Revenue compounds 8-9% for three years before fading; the group margin reaches 34%, roughly legacy Hardie North America economics applied across the combined platform. Capex runs a little higher early to add capacity into the recovery.
scenario_narratives.bear: The housing downturn deepens: FY2027 comes in at the low end of guidance on the strength of the first half already banked, then revenue falls 3% and stalls for a year as new construction and discretionary re-siding/decking both contract and the channel destocks again (the pattern behind the August 2025 guidance cut). Fixed-cost deleverage and freight/input inflation take the margin to 26%, recovering only to 28% - below the pre-AZEK legacy level because decking competes head-on with Trex. Leverage stays above 2x for longer, so the cash flows go to debt rather than buybacks. The securities class action is not separately provisioned in any scenario.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the post-AZEK, post-Europe company on its continuing-operations cash flows from current guidance, not the pre-acquisition record. Charge SBC in the flows, asbestos once in the bridge at the net-of-tax actuarial liability, and add the Fermacell proceeds only because Europe's earnings are out of the flows. Cyclical risk sits in the bear path and its weight; the discount rate is the same across scenarios.
key_risks_to_valuation: The mature Adjusted EBITDA margin (32% base, 28% bear, 34% bull) is the largest driver, and there are only five quarters of combined-company history to anchor it.
Net debt of $3.8bn is about a quarter of base enterprise value, so per-share value moves roughly 1.3x as fast as enterprise value.
Terminal value is most of enterprise value; a 15x cap is in place but Gordon binds at 9.5%/2.5%.
The Fermacell sale ($900m net, about $1.50 a share) has not closed.
Asbestos is carried at the September 2026 central estimate; the actuarial estimate is revised annually and is AUD-denominated.
The securities class action is not provisioned.
AUD/USD: the AUD value moves one-for-one with the exchange rate.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 25.19-44.12 AUD. NYSE primary listing and AUDUSD=X from the same API for the parity check.
data_sources.financials: SEC EDGAR: Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 30 Sep 2026 (accession 0001159152-26-000055) and XBRL company facts for CIK 1159152 (FY2025 20-F, FY2026 10-K, FY2027 10-Qs). JHX.AX_Metrics.csv and the duckdb kpis table for FY2015-FY2024 history.
data_sources.qualitative: JHX.AX_Analysis.json (2026-11-15), including FY2027 guidance as reaffirmed with the Q2 FY2027 result.

inputs.base_revenue_note: Pro forma FY2026 continuing-operations net sales (AZEK for the full year, Europe excluded), derived from FY2027 guidance: $4,990m low end / 1.059 pro forma growth. Reported FY2026 net sales were $4,835.8m including Europe and only nine months of AZEK, so the reported figure is not a usable growth base.
inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted weighted average for the quarter ended 30 Sep 2026 (581.0m basic + 4.8m dilutive stock awards, 10-Q EPS note); 581.6m shares on issue at 30 Sep 2026. Held flat because SBC is expensed in the flows. The 150m-share step from 430m reflects stock issued for AZEK in July 2025 and is already in the count. One ASX CDI represents one ordinary share.
inputs.net_debt_note: Gross debt principal $4,045.3m (10-Q liquidity section; carrying value $4,017.3m after $28.0m issuance costs) plus finance lease liabilities $102.0m, less unrestricted cash $323.1m. Excludes $27.5m restricted cash and $216.1m restricted AICF investments (inside the asbestos bridge item) and $128.7m operating lease liabilities (the rent is an expense inside Adjusted EBITDA).
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 10-K via SEC XBRL: ShareBasedCompensation $38.0m cash-flow add-back plus $13.7m cash paid for shares withheld for taxes (no combined figure published). Forward path anchored on the H1 FY2027 run-rate instead: $34.1m expense in six months on $2,746m of sales (1.2%), plus withholding taxes, rounded up to 1.5%.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2026 (year to 31 Mar 2026): operating cash flow $589.8m less capex $383.9m. Depressed by AZEK acquisition and pre-close financing costs and includes Europe; not a normal year. Reported FCF is already after asbestos claims and handling costs paid (they sit inside consolidated operating cash flow because AICF is consolidated). H1 FY2027 FCF was $535.4m and FY2027 is guided above $650m. Interest income is not stripped: the company is in net debt.
inputs.buyback_note: No repurchases in FY2026 or H1 FY2027 ($149.9m in FY2025, $271.4m in FY2024). A $250m buyback is planned from the Fermacell proceeds. The flat count is therefore a modelling convention the company is not currently funding.
inputs.fx_note: USD to AUD 1.4762 (AUDUSD 0.6774, Yahoo AUDUSD=X, 2026-11-14). Parity check against the NYSE primary listing: JHX closed at US$27.80 on 2026-11-13 21:00Z, x 1.4762 = A$41.04 against the ASX CDI close of A$40.49 sixteen hours earlier, a 1.3% gap explained by the later US session and a 0.5% move in the AUD between the two closes. Direction, rate and the 1:1 CDI ratio all confirmed.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free 4.3% (10-year US Treasury), equity risk premium 5.0%, beta 1.3 for a levered, housing-cyclical building-products maker gives a cost of equity near 10.8%. Debt costs 5.7% pre-tax (weighted average rate in the 10-Q), about 4.3% after tax. At roughly 80/20 equity/debt by market value that is 9.5%. The same rate is used in all three scenarios; cyclicality, leverage and integration risk are carried by the flows and the scenario weights, not by a WACC premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP. Operating lease cost is an operating expense already inside Adjusted EBITDA, so no lease line is deducted and operating lease liabilities ($128.7m) stay out of net debt. Finance leases ($102.0m), whose cost sits in depreciation and interest outside EBITDA, are counted as debt.
inputs.asbestos_treatment: Charged once, through the equity bridge. History: reported operating cash flow and FCF are already net of asbestos claims paid, because AICF is consolidated ($65.2m in H1 FY2027; about $116m in FY2024). Forward: management's Adjusted EBITDA excludes asbestos, so the component flows do not carry it; instead the Net Unfunded AFFA Liability net of tax, $415.2m at 30 Sep 2026 ($701.4m before the $270.3m deferred tax asset and $15.9m tax receivable), is deducted from enterprise value. It is not modelled as a percent-of-revenue charge because the obligation is a finite run-off: capitalising the A$128m FY2027 contribution in the terminal value would charge roughly US$1.2bn after tax, about three times the actuarial liability. The contribution is capped at 35% of the prior year's operating cash flow, so it does not bind at these cash-flow levels.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF (component route) with the non-US/cyclical adaptations. James Hardie is an operating manufacturer; none of the bank, REIT, LIC or distressed routes apply. Reports USD (US GAAP, 10-K/10-Q filer since FY2026), quoted here in AUD as an ASX CDI. STRUCTURAL BREAK: the Metrics CSV and local filings end at FY2024 (March 2024) and describe a different company - before the $8.75bn AZEK acquisition (closed 1 July 2025: shares 430m to 582m, debt $1.1bn to $4.0bn) and before the Europe exit. Pre-acquisition margins, returns and growth are context only. Every anchor and the year-one drivers come from the SEC 10-Q for the quarter ended 30 Sep 2026 (filed 2026-11-05) and SEC XBRL company facts, fetched for this build; they are not yet in the local CSV. Flows are continuing operations only (Europe is a discontinued operation), and the expected Fermacell proceeds are added in the bridge - the matching-asset rule. Adjusted EBITDA is on the company's definition revised 30 June 2026, which excludes share-based compensation, so deducting the SBC line from it charges SBC exactly once. D&A in the tax build is set below the reported 11.5% of sales because about half of reported D&A is amortisation of AZEK intangibles from a largely stock-funded deal, most of it not tax-deductible; the path is depreciation plus the deductible portion. Cash tax starts at 20% (cash taxes paid were $85m in FY2026 and $50m in H1 FY2027, helped by acquisition costs and the interest shield) and ramps to 25%. Working capital consumes 10% of each incremental revenue dollar (receivables plus inventory exceed payables). Not in the model: any settlement of the US securities class action (N.D. Ill. 25-cv-13018), unquantified. The price is a regular ASX close, not an after-hours print.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: the company carries about 2.6x net debt to EBITDA into a housing downturn that management says it is not planning to see end, and has an open securities suit over the last guidance cut. Base 50%: it is guidance for year one and a mid-cycle recovery thereafter. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs a housing recovery, the AZEK commercial synergies and mid-30s margins together, though two consecutive beat-and-raise quarters keep it from going lower.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
